answer: A network can price identity with proof of unique presence instead of proof of key count. Picture validators as willows ringing a lagoon: each one must send a timing signal that reflects off the water and returns in a slot tied to its hardware attestation. One operator running a thousand keys still produces one physical echo per machine, so clones collide on the same return slot and the protocol keeps only the earliest stake-backed claim, throttling the rest to zero weight.
